cloud.failure_mode: Nothing on the device breaks. The BM92 is a Bluetooth-only peripheral with no WiFi and no phone-home of its own; all measurement transfer is local BLE indications, and the Pro app works locally without registering an account. If every Beurer host above went dark tomorrow, the only losses are the app's optional account sync/backup and cross-device history — the monitor keeps measuring and any BLE client speaking the standard Blood Pressure Profile keeps reading it.
cloud.notes: The CDN hosts serve device images under /shared/deviceImages/. Firmware binaries for the BF8x0 WiFi scales were probed at /firmware/bf880.bin on both the CDN and the API host and returned 404 (likely staged on demand or behind the scale's own request path). The BM92 has no firmware-update mechanism at all. Blocking or DNS-redirecting the hmpro/sync hosts does not impair local BLE operation.

device.name: Beurer Series 800 (Premium 800 / BM92) Blood Pressure Monitor
device.notes:
Covers the Beurer BM92, sold in the US as the "Series 800" and "Premium 800" upper-arm blood-pressure monitor (voice output in English/Spanish, 2 users x 120 stored readings, WHO risk classification, cuff-position and arrhythmia indicators). The sister wrist model BC54W advertises as PREMIUM800W and appears to share the same protocol family (app code treats both through the same blood-pressure device path), but only BM92 is documented from app-code evidence here. The US "Deluxe 600" is the older BM82, a sibling in the same HealthManager family.
Headline protocol fact: the BM92 speaks the standard Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure Profile. Saved-measurement transfer is service 0x1810, characteristic 0x2A35 (Blood Pressure Measurement) as INDICATIONS after the client enables the CCCD; there is no custom vendor command protocol for readings. The manual describes automatic transfer after a saved measurement, not cuff control or continuous live-pressure streaming. Time sync is a write of Current Time 0x2A2B on the Current Time Service 0x1805. Device info and battery are the standard DIS 0x180A and BAS 0x180F/0x2A19.
The record layout carries Beurer quirks recovered from the classic app's BM85-family parser and independently documented by smurfix/ble-stuff: the IEEE-11073 SFLOATs are sent BIG-ENDIAN (the app byte-swaps them; smurfix documents the BM85 pulse value arriving with the wrong byte order), the flags byte's bit0 means the values are in kPa and the app multiplies by 7.50061683 to get mmHg, and Beurer appends a user slot byte and a status byte (arrhythmia bit 0x04, bits 6-7 a resting / hemodynamic-stability indicator) past the standard fields. The Pro app's measurement model additionally tracks afib and triple-measurement flags, so BM92-era firmware may carry status bits or trailing bytes the BM85 layout does not describe; whether the payload ends at byte 19 is an open question (see below).
Required companion app is "beurer HealthManager Pro"; the classic "beurer HealthManager" targets the older EU device generation (BM77/BM85/BM96 family) and is documented here mainly as the unobfuscated source of the record format.
There is no OTA/firmware path for the BM92 in either app — firmware update support exists only for the BF880/BF980/BF990 WiFi scales, which self-download from Beurer's server. The two binary blobs bundled in the classic app are activity-tracker (AS-series) display data, not BP-monitor firmware.
Open questions needing hardware: (1) whether the BM92 0x2A35 payload exactly matches the BM85 layout (status at byte 18) or appends extra bytes for the afib/triple flags the Pro app models; (2) bonding type (JustWorks vs passkey) and whether indications require an encrypted link — the app requests OS bonding and no app-level PIN was found; sibling manuals show a passkey on the monitor's display (see device.pairing), unconfirmed for the BM92; (3) whether BM92 actually exposes 0x2A49 Blood Pressure Feature and what it claims; (4) FCC ID (device.report lists a 2023-08-30 filing but is bot-blocked; the printed manual should carry it); (5) whether a user-slot selection write precedes sync — the Pro app has a user-selection view, but its BLE write path could not be established. Physical user selection before inflation is documented in the manual.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The monitor advertises after a measurement or when woken; there is no separate pairing button in the documented flow. Sibling manuals put an automatic-transfer Bluetooth on/off setting in the device's own setup menu (BM 85) — if the monitor never advertises, check that it has not been switched off there.

exclusivity.recovery: If the monitor stops accepting new bonds, remove the OS-level bond on the old phone first. That is the classic single-bond-peripheral symptom rather than a confirmed property of this device.

pairing.notes: The gate is an ordinary link-layer bond with a passkey the monitor displays — the reading that best fits both the app code (it calls the OS bonding API and carries no PIN) and Beurer's own manuals for sibling HealthManager Pro monitors (a PIN appears on the monitor at first connection and is entered on the phone). Low confidence because the BM92's own manual was not available and nobody has watched it pair; the vendor app and account are not involved in the bond itself. One btsnoop capture of a real sync would settle the association model, whether indications need an encrypted link, and whether the monitor holds one bond or several.

pin.notes: Beurer's manuals for HealthManager Pro siblings say the monitor shows a PIN on its own display the first time it connects and the user types it into the phone — the BM 96 manual says so, and the BM 54 manual gives it as six digits. That also explains the app-code finding: neither app contains a PIN of its own because the passkey dialog is the operating system's, raised by the OS bonding call. Not confirmed for the BM92 itself, whose manual could not be retrieved; treat the length as the family's, and size the field from the prompt.

unpair.notes: The phone side is ordinary: forget the monitor in the OS Bluetooth settings and remove it in the app. No source describes clearing the monitor's own record of a bond, and the device has no factory reset established either (see `setup.factory_reset`), so a monitor that refuses a second phone may have no documented way back.

safety_advisory.detail: A third-party client reads measurements the monitor has already taken and stored; it starts nothing, takes no measurement and adds no accuracy of its own. Show systolic, diastolic and pulse exactly as the record carries them, in the unit its flag says (a kPa record must be converted and labelled, never shown as mmHg), with the timestamp and the irregular-heartbeat flag when set. A number that arrived through this spec must never decide a dose, a skipped dose or whether to seek care: the monitor's own display, its instructions for use and a healthcare professional govern. The record layout here is reconstructed from the sister BM85 and not yet confirmed on a BM92, so a field may be wrong. This spec and any client built from it are experimental and unaffiliated with Beurer.
safety_advisory.summary: Blood-pressure readings synced from the monitor are a personal log, not a basis for a medication decision.

credentials.notes: No credentials of any kind: no WiFi, no account token on the device, no pairing PIN. The only shared secret is the OS-level BLE bond key, if bonding encrypts the link.

factory_reset.effect: Not established. Neither app contains a BP-monitor reset procedure, and no hardware was available. Stored state that a reset would presumably clear: the 2x120 measurement memory, user slot configuration, and any bond keys. Consult the printed manual; do not invent a button sequence.

ble.pin_source: None in either app; sibling manuals show a PIN on the monitor display for the OS passkey prompt (unconfirmed for BM92).

methods.description: Enable Bluetooth in the monitor settings, select a user memory, take and save a measurement, then connect during the automatic transfer window and collect saved records over 0x2A35 indications.

steps.action: With the monitor switched on, hold MEMORY to enter settings. The US manual says three seconds; the Pro 1.17.2 tutorial says five seconds.
steps.expect: Device settings open. Inserting batteries also opens them initially.

steps.action: Advance through the settings until the Bluetooth icon flashes, select On with the arrow buttons, and confirm with START/STOP.
steps.expect: Bluetooth transfer enabled. Set a valid date/time before taking offline measurements.

steps.action: Select user memory 1 or 2 with the User button before inflation, then take a measurement and let the result save automatically.
steps.expect: Saved result followed by automatic BLE transfer; do not power off during transfer.

steps.action: Connect to the PREMIUM800 advertisement during transfer and let the OS bond with the device.
steps.notes: The vendor app requests OS bonding. Whether the link must be encrypted before indications flow is an open question.

steps.action: Write the standard CTS Current Time (0x2A2B) so subsequent stored records get correct timestamps.
Enable indications on Blood Pressure Measurement (0x2A35) via its CCCD (0x2902).
steps.expect: One indication per saved record; record count, ordering, and transfer completion behavior remain unverified.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision — no network, no account, no cloud. Enable Bluetooth in the monitor's settings, select user memory 1 or 2 before inflation, and let the monitor save the result. It then transfers the saved measurement automatically; this is not continuous live-pressure streaming. The 2023 US manual says to hold MEMORY for three seconds to reopen settings, while the Pro 1.17.2 tutorial says five seconds; follow the prompt for the actual device/app version. The Pro app requests OS bonding and no app-level PIN exists for blood-pressure devices; sibling manuals have the monitor display a passkey for the OS dialog (see device.pairing; unconfirmed against hardware). It works locally without registering an account.

rejoin.notes: There is no network to rejoin — "rebinding" is just pairing with a new phone. Remove the OS-level bond on the old phone if the device stops accepting new bonds (a common single-bond-peripheral symptom, not yet confirmed on this device).

testing.notes: No hardware was exercised for this spec. The protocol comes from static analysis of the two vendor Android apps (HealthManager Pro and classic HealthManager, both examined 2026-08) plus community documentation of the closely related BM85 record format. The US BM92 manual and Pro workflow were reviewed 2026-11-07: select a user before inflation, save the result, then transfer it locally; this is not continuous pressure streaming. The cloud API version endpoint was probed live on 2026-08-18. The exact BM92 0x2A35 payload tail, bonding type, and the presence of the 0x2A49 Blood Pressure Feature characteristic still need a real capture; no BM92 packet capture has been reviewed.

entities.notes: Arrives as a 0x2A35 indication after the client enables the CCCD, not as a pollable read. Requires SFLOAT decode after the big-endian byte swap, and the kPa->mmHg conversion when the record's flags bit0 is set.

entities.name: Diastolic Pressure
entities.notes: Same indication/decode path as Systolic Pressure.

entities.name: Mean Arterial Pressure
entities.notes: Same indication/decode path as Systolic Pressure.

entities.name: Pulse
entities.notes: Same indication/decode path as Systolic Pressure.

entities.name: User Slot
entities.notes: Which of the 2 on-device user memories the record belongs to.

entities.name: Irregular Heartbeat
entities.notes: Arrhythmia flag from the record status byte; BM85-derived layout, unverified on BM92.

artifacts.description: Static analysis of the beurer HealthManager Pro app (2026-08) — the companion the BM92 pairs with. Package-flattened, obfuscated Kotlin (RxAndroidBle + coroutines). Contributed the advertised name PREMIUM800, the 0x1810 scan filter, the 0x2A35 indication enable, the measurement-sync flow and the CTS 0x1805/0x2A2B time sync. A few key methods (its own 0x2A35 response parser and the user-selection write path) could not be read cleanly, which is why the classic app is the record-format source.

Static analysis of the classic beurer HealthManager app (2026-08) — essentially unobfuscated, and aimed at the older EU device generation (BM77/BM85/BM96 family) rather than the BM92. Its blood-pressure parser is the reference for the record format; it also supplied the CCCD indication-enable path and the family UUID map, and its device-entity tree is where the absence of any BM92 OTA path was confirmed (only the BF8x0 scales carry firmware paths).
Working third-party local reader for the sister BM85 over 0x1810/0x2A35; corroborates the big-endian-SFLOAT quirk.

HTTPS probes 2026-08-18: hmpro.connect.beurer.com /api/v1.1/version returned 200 with Health Manager Pro API 1.14.2 (build 20260218); sync.connect-beurer.com responding; firmware paths for the BF8x0 scales 404 on both CDN and API hosts.

covers: post-measurement saved-record transfer (systolic/diastolic/MAP/pulse/timestamp/user slot) via 0x2A35 indications
not_covered: cuff inflation and continuous live pressure — no 0x2A2C intermediate-pressure path or remote measurement trigger is established
a dedicated download-all-history gesture — powering on an already-paired monitor is not proven to export all missed records
cloud account sync/backup across devices (inherently a vendor-cloud feature, and optional)
local_access.notes: smurfix/ble-stuff demonstrates third-party local sync of the sister BM85 with no vendor cloud, over the identical 0x1810/0x2A35 path. That supports the local route but does not establish BM92 history coverage or payload details without a BM92 capture.
local_access.summary: Local by design: the monitor speaks the standard Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure Profile over BLE and has no other radio. A BP-profile client with the Beurer byte-order and unit handling can receive saved records without the vendor cloud; the complete BM92 flow remains untested.

format.name: flags
format.notes: bit0 (0x01): values in kPa (multiply decoded SFLOAT values by 7.50061683 for mmHg). bit1 (0x02): 7-byte timestamp present at bytes 7-13. Remaining bits per the SIG profile; not verified against BM92 traffic.

format.name: systolic_sfloat
format.notes: IEEE-11073 SFLOAT sent big-endian (Beurer quirk; swap bytes, then decode 12-bit two's-complement mantissa + 4-bit two's-complement exponent). Unit is mmHg unless flags bit0 says kPa.

format.name: diastolic_sfloat
format.notes: Same big-endian SFLOAT encoding as systolic_sfloat.

format.name: map_sfloat
format.notes: Mean arterial pressure, same big-endian SFLOAT encoding.

format.name: year
format.notes: Present only when flags bit1 is set. Little-endian — the one little-endian multi-byte field in the record.

format.name: pulse_sfloat
format.notes: Pulse rate, big-endian SFLOAT; high byte observed as zero in the BM85 documentation, so the value effectively fits in one byte.

format.name: user_slot
format.notes: Which of the device's 2 user memories the record belongs to.

format.name: reserved_17
format.notes: Unused in the BM85 layout; BM92 may use it — unverified.

format.name: status
format.notes: bit2 (0x04) = irregular heartbeat / arrhythmia detected. bits 6-7 = resting (HSD / hemodynamic stability) indicator: 00 = insufficient rest, 01 (bit6 set) = sufficient rest. BM92-era firmware may define additional bits (afib, triple measurement) per the Pro app's model — unverified.

characteristics.name: Blood Pressure Measurement
characteristics.notes:
Standard Blood Pressure Measurement characteristic, sent as saved- record indications once the client writes 0x0002 (enable indications) to its CCCD. Payload is the IEEE-11073-style blood-pressure record with Beurer quirks, recovered from the classic app's BM85-family parser and independently documented by smurfix/ble-stuff:
- All SFLOATs are BIG-ENDIAN (both apps byte-swap them; the SIG
  profile is little-endian, so a standards-conformant decoder
  misreads every value — smurfix documents exactly this on the
  BM85 pulse field).
- Flags byte 0 bit0 = values are in kPa; the app converts with
  x * 7.50061683 to mmHg. Bit1 = the 7-byte timestamp is present.
- Systolic/diastolic/MAP are SFLOAT pairs at bytes 1-6. - Timestamp (when flag bit1 set) is year as little-endian uint16
  then month/day/hour/minute/second bytes — the one field that is
  little-endian.
- Pulse is a big-endian SFLOAT at bytes 14-15 (high byte zero). - Byte 16 is the user slot; byte 17 is unused in the BM85 layout;
  byte 18 is a status byte: bit2 (0x04) = irregular
  heartbeat/arrhythmia detected, bits 6-7 = resting ("HSD",
  hemodynamic stability) indicator, 00 = insufficient rest,
  01 = sufficient rest.
- UNVERIFIED for BM92 specifically: the Pro app's measurement
  model also tracks afib and triple-measurement flags, so
  BM92-era firmware may append bytes past 19 or use additional
  status bits. One btsnoop capture of a sync settles this.

characteristics.name: Blood Pressure Feature
characteristics.notes: Standard BP Feature characteristic; the classic app's family table lists 0x2A49 for the BP family. Whether the BM92 actually exposes it (and whether it claims kPa support, which would tell a client to expect flags bit0 set) is UNVERIFIED — open question pending a hardware capture.

services.name: Blood Pressure Service
services.notes: Standard Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure Service 0x1810. This is the documented saved-measurement transfer surface: the client enables indications on 0x2A35 and the device sends saved records (the app enables the CCCD 0x2902 for indication, not notification). The same service/characteristic pair serves the entire Beurer BP family (BM54/57/75/77/81/85/93/96, BC54, SRBM1/788) per the classic app's supported-services table, which is why the BM85 record parser is the reference for the format below.

set_current_time.description: Sync the device clock (standard CTS Current Time write)

adjust_reason.description: CTS adjust-reason bitmask; bit0 = manual time update.

fractions256.description: Sub-second fraction in 1/256 s units; 0 is fine for a clock sync.

year_high.description: High byte of the little-endian uint16 year (e.g. 2026 -> 0x07).

year_low.description: Low byte of the little-endian uint16 year (e.g. 2026 -> 0xEA).

characteristics.name: Current Time
characteristics.notes: Standard CTS Current Time write, 10 bytes: year (LE uint16), month, day, hour, minute, second, day-of-week (1=Monday .. 7=Sunday), fractions-of-second (1/256 s), adjust-reason bitmask. Little-endian throughout per the SIG specification.

services.name: Current Time Service
services.notes: Standard CTS 0x1805. Both apps sync the device clock by writing Current Time 0x2A2B in the standard CTS format. Whether BM92 also accepts vendor-specific configuration writes (e.g. a user-slot selection before download — the Pro app has a user-selection screen whose backing BLE write could not be read cleanly) is an open question.

format.name: model_number
format.notes: Maximum length unverified; standard UTF-8 model string.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard DIS 0x180A as listed in the apps' device-info handling.
